subject: english
title: Ac：字彙

content.summary: 本課聚焦「字彙」，以自編範例練習概念、證據與新情境遷移。

sections.heading: 學習目標
sections.body: 能根據題目提供的條件、資料或情境，辨識並說明「字彙」相關的關係。

sections.heading: 學習流程
sections.body: 先讀出題幹中與「字彙」有關的條件；再以自己的話整理判斷依據；最後回到題目檢查結論。

sections.heading: 常見錯誤
sections.body: 不要只因看到「字彙」的名稱就作答；必須確認題幹證據與結論是否一致。

sections.heading: 自我檢核
sections.body: 嘗試在新情境中說明何時適用「字彙」，並指出至少一項支持判斷的條件。

studyHighlights: 先圈出與「字彙」直接相關的條件。
用自己的話說出判斷依據，不靠答案位置或關鍵字猜測。
回到原題檢查結論是否符合所有限制與資料。

assessmentEmphasis: 要求用上下文、搭配、詞性與拼字證據支持詞義判斷。

body.heading: A lost-and-found note needs better words
body.body: The school office has posted a short note: “A blue bottle was found near the music room. Please tell Ms. Lin if it is yours.” A student changes found to find and writes “tell to Ms. Lin,” so the reader is unsure what happened and whom to contact. Read the note once for its purpose, then circle the words that show an object, an action, a place, or a person. Do not translate every word separately. Ask what the writer wants the reader to do, and mark one word whose meaning you can infer from the surrounding sentence. This is the first lesson of vocabulary: a word becomes useful when it helps a real reader build a clear message.

body.heading: A word carries more than a Chinese gloss
body.body: To understand a vocabulary item, check five clues: its spelling, its part of speech, the words that commonly stand beside it, the sentence situation, and the writer’s purpose. In “Please record your name,” record is an action; in “Keep a record of the meeting,” it is a thing. The Chinese translation may change, but the grammar and nearby words tell us how the item works. Spelling families such as act, action, and active can suggest a relationship, yet they are not interchangeable in every sentence. Pronunciation can help you remember a word, but a sound alone cannot decide its spelling or meaning. Treat each guess as a hypothesis and return to the whole sentence to test it.

body.heading: Repairing the club announcement
body.body: Consider this original announcement: “The art club meets on Friday. Bring a pencil and a small notebook. New members can join at the library.” First, sort meet, bring, member, and join into action words and people or things. Next, use the time, place, and object clues to explain each word without copying a dictionary translation. Now change one detail: the meeting moves to Tuesday and the room changes to the science lab. Rewrite only the sentences that must change, then read the whole announcement as a new student. If you write “members joins,” the problem is subject–verb agreement; if you write “in Tuesday,” the problem is the word partnership with a day. The final check is whether a reader can act correctly, not whether every word has a one-to-one Chinese gloss.

body.heading: The vocabulary workshop
body.body: Work with four original cards: “The gate is open,” “Open your notebook,” “The shop is close,” and “Please close the door.” Put open and close into a word network, but do not assume that the same spelling always has the same grammatical job. Label each card as a description or a command, underline the nearby noun or object, and say what the reader should understand or do. Then replace one card with a picture and ask a partner to rebuild the sentence from the picture and a word bank. When a partner chooses close for “The shop is ___,” point to the sentence pattern and meaning rather than saying only “wrong.” Record the evidence used: word position, nearby word, situation, and spelling.

body.heading: One message, three readers
body.body: Use the same facts—“The green umbrella is at the front desk. Ask Mr. Wu before you take it.”—to make three versions: a quick text to a friend, a polite office note, and a short announcement for visitors. Decide what each reader needs first. Keep the key vocabulary accurate, but change the level of detail and politeness. Exchange versions with another group; the reader must identify the object, location, owner or contact person, and next action without asking the writer. If the reader confuses green with a person’s name or take with bring, revise the surrounding words and sentence, not just the translation list. This transfer activity shows that knowing a word means choosing it appropriately for a purpose and an audience.

body.heading: A final vocabulary audit
body.body: Choose one unfamiliar word from an original notice and explain your decision in four moves: point to the sentence clue, identify its likely part of speech, test a nearby word partnership, and use the word in a new sentence. Then check the spelling letter by letter and ask a classmate who has not seen your answer to read the message. If the classmate understands a different meaning, write down which clue was missing or misleading. Remember the boundary of the method: context can guide a reasonable guess, but it cannot prove every dictionary meaning or pronunciation. A strong vocabulary learner can revise a word, a sentence, or the message purpose, and can explain why the revision helps the next reader.

summary: 先用自己的話界定「字彙」的關鍵概念與適用條件。
